Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
I considered for a long time before I chose this grill. I wanted something compact (hence the fold-down side table) that wouldn't take up much space on my porch. I also wanted something that would last for "the rest of our lives", as my husband and I are "seniors".
A third feature is ease of lighting.
A bonus I hadn't counted on, but have been delighted to find is the even, consistent heating. And it heats FAST, also!

I have been assembling grills as a job for the last three years, and I've seen a lot of different brands and models. NONE of the other grills has the quality of materials as the Webers. This explains why they can offer the best warranty in the industry. (I suspect some brands are just hoping folks won't make good on their warranties, because you can tell they won't last.)
My only complaint is the plastic knobs for the burners. (another Weber grill has metal ones, so I don't know why ALL their models don't)

Ease of cleaning was another consideration, since I intend this grill to serve into my elder years. So far I've found if I clean each time I use it, (something motivated by the price our kids paid to get this for Father's Day), it is easy to clean. NO grill should be neglected and not cleaned, or it becomes very hard to clean. The grease tray is easy to reach and remove, and if I were so inclined, I could buy replacement tray liners, and just dispose of the liner each time, instead of emptying it.

If you are considering a grill, think about how this Weber will outlast 3 or 4 other grills, so it's worth the investment!
Results.Title: Best Choice!

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
This is not my first Webber gas grill. My previous ones lasted 10+ years each.

The good:
(1) The grill lights easily. The newer ignition module that takes an AA battery keeps clicking as long as you hold down the button. With the older piezo igniter you had to push repeatedly if it didn’t catch the first time.
(2) The (cast iron it looks like, with a surface treatment of some kind) grill surface seems to be more “spatula friendly” in that it is flatter on top. Time will tell if it is as durable as the old “continuous cleaning” stamped steel grill surface.
(3) The grilling surface seems large enough for all but large gatherings - read the description, it gives the grill area.
(4) The quality seems to be what I expect from Webber.

Needs Improvement:
(1) Assembly is a real pain. In order to fit into a smaller box, there were more smaller pieces of the frame parts which meant it seemed like there were nearly twice as many pieces in the box to assemble than my old Webber Genesis Silver had been. While the instructions are clear enough, you have to pay a lot of attention to which way certain parts are oriented as there are subtle differences in symmetry between left and right parts for example - And I am a retired engineer! It takes two people to assemble this, by the way. It would be difficult for one person to do all the steps.
(2) While I like the continuous re-strike ignition of the newer battery operated ignition module verses the older piezo igniter, I have a concern with battery life in an outdoor appliance like this. It uses a single AA battery. At least it’s easy enough to change. And by the way, the battery that came with it was dead because it had been packed bare inside a plastic bag of metal screws and hardware that obviously shorted out the original battery in transit.

All in all, once assembled the grill is easy to use and seems to be of good quality. But assembly is a real pain.
Results.Title: Great Grill - Assembly Is A Pain

Results.ReviewText:
I like --
the grill base made of heavy metal that is easy to clean
the heavy porcelain-enameled cooking grates that don't rust
the fuel gauge that shows how rapidly the grill heats up
the crossover ignition that minimizes use of the electronic ignition button
the easy access to the LP tank
the LP tank gauge that shows how much of the LP gas is left in the tank

I already had to replace the control knobs on the grill.
These are a little flimsy.
Unless you remember to push the control knob in first before turning, the control knobs will strip and need to be replaced.
However, I was pleased to have the control knobs replaced at no cost.

Results.ReviewText: I had a Weber gas grill for 10 years or so and was very happy with it, but it was time for a new one.  I chose the Spirit II E-210 for its size and price.  It's an excellent grill and I'm very happy with it.  The only thing that keeps me from giving a 5 star rating is that the shape and construction of the lid forces grilling smoke back into my face.  My old grill opened far enough that any smoke went straight up, bypassing the lid and me.  But the lid of this new one draws the smoke in and then it rolls back out, into my face.  I learned quickly though so now I back up when I open the lid.

44010001.Description:
Open the door to the world of grilling with crazy good food and friends coming together. Equipped with the powerful GS4 grilling system, this two burner gas grill is your entry to the Weber family and to everyday grilling. The compact open-cart design and the practical folding side table makes it fit even on small spaces, and you have all the basics you need to get familiar with gas grilling. So whether it’s a busy Monday or a relaxed Sunday – invite a couple of friends over, push the ignition and enjoy the special atmosphere that surrounds the grill.


 This product requires assembly.
